reviewer.notes: Independent re-derivation from live probe1.raw.txt and probe2.raw.txt, not from the harvest UNIT-COMPLETE badge. Probe 1: pristine mirror and bundle installs completed 13/13 gates; one-byte payload mutations were refused at MKT-I09 with no installed payload; verify_bundle/import_bundle accepted the tampered bundle. Probe 2: offline-bundle schema requires index_digest/manifest_digest/payload_digest; digestless mutant rejected; round trip preserved signed metadata; maintainer and publisher keys are distinct pinned trust anchors. Wrong-gate mutant expecting MKT-I08 exited 1.

defects.summary: verify_bundle/import_bundle authenticate the envelope and declared digest relationships but do not recompute package payload bytes before copying; tamper is refused only when Installer later runs gate 9.

Named probe scripts and sidecar raw logs were absent on the harvest checkout. Restored probe1_install_tamper.py and probe2_format_audit.py, re-ran them to exit 0, and registered the catalog output_path in the per-unit UNIT-ARTIFACT-MANIFEST.json.

retry.policy: Two implement-and-remeasure strikes. Named probes restored and re-ran; receipt packed only after live exit 0.

residual_unknowns.claim: Only the implemented filesystem mirror/bundle substrate was measured; there is no network transport in mkt, so HTTP cache/proxy mutation and download-stream TOCTOU behavior are outside this result.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: When a remote transport exists, serve the same one-byte mutation through a local HTTP proxy before and during download, and require refusal plus zero installed residue in both timing windows.

report.refutation_basis: Both named probes were executed again from the real marketplace fixture, the wrong-gate detector mutant went red with exit 1, and the live condition-11 check was captured without invoking write mode.
report.question_or_target: If a private mirror or an offline export bundle serves modified content, does the client detect it - and does the export/import round trip preserve integrity metadata at all?
report.answer: YES at install time, but NOT at the bundle import boundary. A one-byte change from either mirror or imported bundle was refused by Installer at MKT-I09 and left no installed payload. verify_bundle/import_bundle accepted and copied the changed bundle payload. Integrity rests on consumer-pinned, distinct Ed25519 registry-maintainer and publisher keys.
report.evidence_requirement: Probe 1: install from the tampered mirror and from the tampered bundle and record whether the tamper is detected, with the artifact hash as evidence. Probe 2 (mechanically different): inspect the export format for integrity metadata; a format with no digest field cannot detect tampering regardless of what the install attempt happens to do.
named_probes_verbatim: Probe 1: install from the tampered mirror and from the tampered bundle and record whether the tamper is detected, with the artifact hash as evidence.
Probe 2 (mechanically different): inspect the export format for integrity metadata; a format with no digest field cannot detect tampering regardless of what the install attempt happens to do.

targets.answer: Yes: REFUSED at payload-digest with MKT-I09; no payload was installed.

targets.question: Does verify_bundle/import_bundle itself detect a one-byte payload change before copying it?
targets.answer: No: both returned success and the imported file hash equaled the tampered bundle hash.

targets.question: Does a downstream install from the imported tampered bundle detect the content change?
targets.answer: Yes: REFUSED at payload-digest with MKT-I09; no payload was installed.

targets.question: Does the export/import round trip preserve integrity metadata?
targets.answer: Yes: package-manifest bytes, manifest_digest, payload_digest, and signed per-file hashes were preserved.

targets.question: Is integrity anchored outside the process that computes the offline bundle digest?
targets.answer: Yes: consumer pins the registry maintainer key for bundle/index signatures and a distinct publisher key for the signed package manifest.

refutation_basis: Both named probes were executed again from the real marketplace fixture, the wrong-gate detector mutant went red with exit 1, and the live condition-11 check was captured without invoking write mode.
question_or_target: If a private mirror or an offline export bundle serves modified content, does the client detect it - and does the export/import round trip preserve integrity metadata at all?
answer: YES at install time, but NOT at the bundle import boundary. A one-byte change from either mirror or imported bundle was refused by Installer at MKT-I09 and left no installed payload. verify_bundle/import_bundle accepted and copied the changed bundle payload. Integrity rests on consumer-pinned, distinct Ed25519 registry-maintainer and publisher keys.
evidence_requirement: Probe 1: install from the tampered mirror and from the tampered bundle and record whether the tamper is detected, with the artifact hash as evidence. Probe 2 (mechanically different): inspect the export format for integrity metadata; a format with no digest field cannot detect tampering regardless of what the install attempt happens to do.

targets.answer: No: both returned success and the imported file hash equaled the tampered bundle hash.

targets.answer: Yes: REFUSED at payload-digest with MKT-I09; no payload was installed.

targets.answer: Yes: consumer pins the registry maintainer key for bundle/index signatures and a distinct publisher key for the signed package manifest.
